TOW TRUCKERS EXPOSED

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose a tow truck company conning clients by towing their wheels fraudulently and holding them to ransom.

Summary:
A1 Assist cons clients into believing they are authorised by the client’s insurance company to tow the smashed car. But when it comes to collecting your car for repairs, the truth is revealed… Your insurance has no record of the claim, and you’re being held to by A1 Assist – if you want your wheels – pay up!

Further information:
BACKGROUND
This seems to be A1 Assist standard operating procedure. We have at least 5 case studies of our own and an additional 21 cases on HelloPeter for the last year (some as recent as February). There is a clear thread – we’ve got your car, if you want it, pay up!

INSIDER INTERVIEW
I have an insider that will spill the beans on the MO, confirming this is a tactic used by tow truck drivers to secure business.

CASE STUDIES
Below are three recent and most relevant case studies that are willing to go on camera – they have all the documentation and pics from the accident scenes. Some even tried to take legal action against A1 Assist.

CASE STUDY ONE
RAINER WODRICH’s 19 year old daughter was in a car accident on the 10th of October 2015. First to the scene was A1 assist, Rainer’s daughter was being attended to by paramedics having hurt her back and was about to taken to the emergency room.

“A-1 Assist Tow-Truck (but with Help-U 24 Signage) arrived on the scene within minutes, and offered to tow the vehicle. I initially refused, telling them I would need to get authorization from my insurance. However, I told the Tow-Truck operator who I was insured with.

A few minutes later, the operator handed me his phone, and the voice on the other end told me that he had contacted the insurance company, and he had authorization to tow the vehicle. I did not take the details of the other person on the phone, but he repeatedly assured me that he had obtained authorization.

I again asked the tow-truck operator about the costs, and he assured me that because they had authorization, the insurance would cover the costs. For this reason there was nothing filled in regarding costs on the Tow Authorization and Invoice document.

I then asked the Tow-Truck operator where they were towing the vehicle to, and his response was the Roodepoort Assessment Centre, where the insurance assessor wouldcome to have a look. I asked him why, because I only have fire, theft and 3rd part insurance on the vehicle, and why could they not take it to my home, about 2 Km away, also in Randpark Ridge. His response was that he had to take it to the Assessment Centre in Roodepoort because the assessor will need to see the vehicle, no matter what! He absolutely refused to take it to my home.”

When he contacted A1 Assist to enquire about whether the assessor had been to see the car and what the way forward was, a lady informed Rainer that there had never been any insurance authorization, and he would have to pay a release fee of R8,300-00 to get the vehicle back!

He checked with his insurance company aand they insurance subsequently confirmed that they had never been contacted and there had never been any authorization given at all, and this was all my responsibility because towing is not part of the third party, fire and theft cover on the car.

He eventually got hold of a manager named Hennie, and after much begging, got him to reduce the cost from the original R8300-00 to R5200-00, still an exorbitant amount.
After the money was paid to him, they delivered the car at his home almost two weeks after the accient, but the battery was missing, the fuel tank was empty and the additional spotlights I had installed on the car, and which were not damaged, were gone!

This is an unscrupulous bunch of people taking advantage of innocent people at their time of distress, and extorting money from them because they are unaware of the trap they are walking into.

CASE STUDY TWO
THAMI MADLALA…
“I was involved in accident on the 11th of January and in less than no time, there were tow trucks around my car. I then told the driver of the tow truck that I don't have insurance and how much would it be if he had to tow my car. He then informed me that the yard charges R350 per day and that I can fetch the car the following day. when I arrived at the storage to inquire about the amount I need to pay, they told me it would be around R9000 because of a number of things like towing fees, storage, etc.”

Thami’s car is still with A1 Assist and his bill is sitting in the region of R20 000.00

CASE STUDY THREE
ANTOINETTE TILL
Had an accident on Witkoppen Road on 29th October 2015. The A1 Assist tow truck driver pretended to call her insurance company to get an authorisation number. She was also handed the phone and spoke to some fictitious call centre person to confirm her details and get authorisation.
The staff at their offices perpetuate the fraud by giving you a refence number for the tow, but it was later revealed that no authorisation was given. Her insurance would only pay R1500 and she was liable for the balance of R3500 of the A1 account.

WHY ARE PEOPLE BEING CAUGHT?
The tow truckers get a ficticious person to pretend that they are the client’s insurance company – often giving back details like the car make and registration number – these details would have been given to the so-called call centre agent by the tow truck driver. Believing it’s all legitimate, the client signs A1 Assist’s towing agreement, the car is handed over and towed away. Only when the client makes follow up enquiries with their insurance company it is revealed that they have been scammed and no claim or call to them insurance was logged.

By then it’s too late and the client’s car is being held by A1 Assist and the only way to get your car back is to pay up!

CAN THEY BE CAUGHT?
I’d like to do a sting operation, faking a minor accident. I’ll claim that I drove through a pothole and it looks like the suspension is broken. We’ll call in A1 Assist to attend to the accident and let it unfold. We’ll go to collect the car the next day with presenter and cameras rolling.

We’ll also take Thami Madlala with and try to retrieve his car.

EXPERT INTERVIEW
We’ll Interview the South African Insurance Crime Bureau about these kinds of cases to show how widespread the problem is and to get some advice for consumers.




Extra Budget Items:
We might need to cover the cost of getting the car released as was the case in the Big Truck Flip story. I am going to try to get a car loan, we might be liable if there is any damage or parts stolen.

Press Release:


Tow Trucks
Some tow truckers often con clients into believing they are authorised by the client’s insurance company to tow their smashed car. But when the time comes to collect the car for repairs, the truth is revealed. Your insurance has no record of the so-called authorisation, and you’re held to ransom – if you want your wheels, pay up! Carte Blanche investigates and finds a surprising twist in the tale.


Script:


STRUCTURE TOW TRUCKS 2016

VO: There are over 10 million vehicles on South African roads. With one of the highest accident rates in the world, it’s pretty much guaranteed that you’ll have to deal with a tow trucker at some stage in your life.

Tow truck drivers don’t have the best reputation, often called vultures, waiting for accidents to happen.

LINK: This is a quantity business, the more cars you bring in the more you get paid, so some drivers will go to any lenghts to get that tow…

ANTOINETTE: I had no reason to believe that someone would be taking me for the biggest ride of my life after I had just been in a crash

VO: Despite the tow truck industry’s efforts to clean up operations, there are still a number of rogue drivers that take chances, says Garth De Klerk from the South African Insurance Crime Bureau.

GARTH: They are very smooth, a tow truck operator on a scene can be consoling, can be very gentle and they can really lure you into a false sense of security – so you trust them.

VO: While most insured consumers know that they need to contact their insurance company to get authorisation to tow the car – dodgy truck drivers also know these rules, and are finding creative ways to bend them.

Something Antoinette Till learnt the hard way, when she was in major accident involving two other cars, north of Johannesburg in October last year.

ANTOINETTE: I was shaking like a leaf, I’d gotten a big fright, I mean, I had walked out of car that was completely squashed on the driver’s side, without a scratch

VO: She took us to the scene of the accident.

UPSOUND CAR: It happened right over there….

VO: Antoinette didn’t have her insurance details on her, and says she was rattled by the accident not knowing what do to first.

LINK: Like knights in shining armour the tow truck drivers come out of nowhere, they take charge out of the situation, you’ve just been in an accident, they hand you a phone and assure you that the person on the other side is from your insurance company

ANTOINETTE: I spoke to a person, // he was very helpful over the phone, and I could hear tapping of keyboard keys and papers ruffling, and he said he would give the reference number to the towtruck driver.

VO: But there was no authorisation number, because the person she spoke to was an imposter, he was NOT from her insurance company – Antoinette was being conned.

She was later slapped with a bill of R5000 – pay up or the car doesn’t get released!

Although Execuline Insurance covered Antoinette for towing, they did not have an agreement with this company.

This is not an isolated case.

LINK: We’ve received a number of complaints, and all them are pointing to the same MO and they’re pointing the finger at A1 assist. LINK 3

VO: A1 assist is part of the Help24 Group of Companies.

GARTH: We have had complaints as regards to that specific company recently,
BONGANI: how far are you investigations?
GARTH: They’re at a sensitive point at this stage
BONGANI: Is this just an ordinary scam or could this be considered a crime?
GARTH: It’s a crime, if you are in any way was misleading an individual with the intention of deceiving them or taking money off them – those are different levels of crimes, it’s fraud.

VO: When Rainer Wodrich’s daughter was in accident last year, he rushed to the scene – he was also met by helpful tow truckers, who also claimed to have placed a call to his insurance company.

BONGANI: at the time, didn’t that strike you as strange?
RAINER: You know Bongani, `I must be honest, I didn’t even think about it at that stage, it’s only afterwards that it struck me that they should not have towed the vehicle at all, the insurance would not have authorised any towing as it’s not part of the cover for that particular vehicle.

VO: Garth says this is the standard Modus Operandi.

GARTH: They mislead into the individual that they have cover and they are porviding a service which has been approved by the person’s insurance company. The car is then hooked up and then transferred to a lot and then that car is basically held for ransom where there are high fees involved.

VO: Rainer’s bill came to R8200!

RAINER: Literally for just towing my vehicle to a destination I didn’t even want them to take it to in the first place. I wanted them to take it to my home which is 2, 2 and half kilometers from here.
BONGANI: that’s crazy!
RAINER: That’s absolute extortion, and these guys are slick and they know what they are doing, and they are taking money off innocent people in bad situations.

VO: Pleading poverty Rainer managed knock off 3 grand - he coughed up R5000 in the end to get the car back.

Antoinette’s insurance gave her R1500 towards the bill – she parted with R3500 to get her wheels released.

We decided to put A1 Assist to the test.

This is our sting car, we’ve staged an accident, we took off the wheel, and created the impression that suspension was damaged.

LINK: There is a massive pothole behind us, no one is driving away from here. So now we are going to call them and let’s see if they’ll take the bait. LINK 5

VO: We called in the breakdown, and within minutes A1 Assist were on the scene. Tow truck driver, Derrick concluded a tow would be necessary.
UPSOUND UNDERCOVER:
DERRICK: When you hit the pothole, the suspension is gone…

VO: He was playing by the rules.
UPSOUND UNDERCOVER:
DERRICK: Can’t just tow without an authorisation, we can’t just tow it to a yard, those scruffy companies aren’t here anymore.

VO: He even called in his manager Marius to assist, he was also not interested in bending the rules.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER:
OPERATIVE: I think it’s Execuline…
MARIUS: We don’t tow Execuline – they only work with the AA

VO: But without an authorisation, they were not taking the bait - it was time to tell them they had passed the test.

BONGANI: we wanted to see if you guys would follow the rules, you guys did well, you passed the test… that’s a good thing.
MARIUS: Yes, it is. Becaue of a handful drivers that make mistakes and con people we all get given a bad name.

VO: While these towtruckers passed the test this time, we still had enough complaints against A1 Assist to warrant a visit to the big boss.

Company Director, Rudi Steynberg agreed to meet with us at their storage yard. The company tows over 300 cars a week with almost 200 drivers on the road – he says these complaints are the exception not the rule.

RUDI: You’re not on the accident scene, and we don’t always know what happens on the accident scene, like I said, there are a lot of people that think they’ve got insurance or they think they’re covered in certain cases and they’re not.

VO: But that wasn’t Antoinette’s scenario – she had comprehensive insurance, but A1 Assist was not an authorised company registered with her insurance.

RUDI: There should have been a tow truck driver’s and the registration on that invoice….
BONGANI: nothing, no number, no driver’s registration…nada….
RUDI: this is a case that I will look into, it’s not supposed to happen like that….

VO: He promised the same with Rainer’s case.

BONGANI: It’s one thing to say you are going to look at these cases, but what actions are you actually going to take?
RUDI: Bongani, I am going to take action right now in these cases. I will investigate the drivers, and I will have a disciplinary with the drivers

VO: Garth says tow truck drivers are often the biggest culprits. Accident victims don’t realise that they not only have responsiblities but they have rights too.

GARTH: You have the right to phone your insurance company to get another operator to come on the scene and remove your vehicle at the insurance’s costs.

VO: But for people like Thami Madlala who had no insurance, his options were limited. Thami says he was relieved when the tow truck driver came to his rescue in January this year.

THAMI: They gave me authorisation to tow your car.They would pay for everything as a third party claim…

VO: Thami was told he would only be responsible one day’s storage at a cost of R350.

THAMI: I got here with the R350 to take my car my back and then she told me I need to pay for the towing fee, administration fee… The lady then told me now, me I need to pay 8.7, 9000. She was like it’s either you pay the 9000 or you give us your car papers and we buy the car from you.

VO: Unable to come up with the cash, two months later his car was still at yard, with his bill sitting at a whopping R30 000!

We introduced Thami to Rudi.

BONGANI: He came here the next day wanting his car, he still wants his car…

RUDI: We still deliver a service, but R8000 is too much, we don’t charge that kind of money. I will have to look into myself
BONGANI: This isn’t just one or two people – your reputation is on the line.
RUDI: It’s unacceptable for me as well, as a member of the public, we’re a company that operates mostly in Gauteng, we are here to assist clients and insurance companies to clients vehicles to the right destination – that is our core business. I don’t want to be labelled with complaints like this

VO: Rudi dealt with Thami’s complaint while we were still there…

RUDI: we’re going to deliver, give you car free of charge…
BONGANI: when? Today
RUDI: YAH.

VO: While Thami got his wheels back, there is an important lesson for consumers to learn.

GARTH: so, it’s very important that people the responsibility that what is verbally agreed to is written down. You are signing a legal document for a contract to remove your vehicle. If that is verbally agreed – you’ve got nothing to fall back on, you have no protection.

VO: For Rainer, it’s a lessson that came at great cost.

RAINER: // other road users // must know that they must be very, very careful when they select a tow truck operator.Don’t allow any rogue to come and take your car away, you may not see it again.


PROMOS
10 second promo

VO: The tow truck industy is a quantity business, the more cars you bring in the more you get paid - opening the door for dodgy drivers to con accident victims, holding their cars for ransom.

15 second promo 1

VO: Dodgy tow truckers bend the rules secure the tow - conning accident victims to sign on the dotted line at the scene - then knocking them with exorbitant bills the next day.

RAINER: Don’t allow any rogue to come and take your car away, you may not see it again.

15 second promo 2
VO: Some Tow truckers operate like vultures, targeting vulnerable accident victims.

GARTH: They are very smooth, // and they can really lure you into a false sense of security.

LINK: Like knights in shining armour the tow truck drivers come out of nowhere, they take charge out of the situation, you’ve just been in an accident, they hand you a phone and assure you that the person on the other side is from your insurance company ANTOINETTE: I spoke to a person, // he was very helpful over the phone, and I could hear tapping of keyboard keys and papers ruffling, and he said he would give the reference number to the towtruck driver. VO: But there was no authorisation number, because the person she spoke to was an imposter, he was NOT from her insurance company – Antoinette was being conned. She was later slapped with a bill of R5000 – pay up or the car doesn’t get released! Although Execuline Insurance covered Antoinette for towing, they did not have an agreement with this company. This is not an isolated case. LINK: We’ve received a number of complaints, and all them are pointing to the same MO and they’re pointing the finger at A1 assist. LINK 3 VO: A1 assist is part of the Help24 Group of Companies. GARTH: We have had complaints as regards to that specific company recently, BONGANI: how far are you investigations? GARTH: They’re at a sensitive point at this stage BONGANI: Is this just an ordinary scam or could this be considered a crime? GARTH: It’s a crime, if you are in any way was misleading an individual with the intention of deceiving them or taking money off them – those are different levels of crimes, it’s fraud. VO: When Rainer Wodrich’s daughter was in accident last year, he rushed to the scene – he was also met by helpful tow truckers, who also claimed to have placed a call to his insurance company. BONGANI: at the time, didn’t that strike you as strange? RAINER: You know Bongani, `I must be honest, I didn’t even think about it at that stage, it’s only afterwards that it struck me that they should not have towed the vehicle at all, the insurance would not have authorised any towing as it’s not part of the cover for that particular vehicle. VO: Garth says this is the standard Modus Operandi. GARTH: They mislead into the individual that they have cover and they are porviding a service which has been approved by the person’s insurance company. The car is then hooked up and then transferred to a lot and then that car is basically held for ransom where there are high fees involved. VO: Rainer’s bill came to R8200! RAINER: Literally for just towing my vehicle to a destination I didn’t even want them to take it to in the first place. I wanted them to take it to my home which is 2, 2 and half kilometers from here. BONGANI: that’s crazy! RAINER: That’s absolute extortion, and these guys are slick and they know what they are doing, and they are taking money off innocent people in bad situations. VO: Pleading poverty Rainer managed knock off 3 grand - he coughed up R5000 in the end to get the car back. Antoinette’s insurance gave her R1500 towards the bill – she parted with R3500 to get her wheels released. We decided to put A1 Assist to the test. This is our sting car, we’ve staged an accident, we took off the wheel, and created the impression that suspension was damaged. LINK: There is a massive pothole behind us, no one is driving away from here. So now we are going to call them and let’s see if they’ll take the bait. LINK 5 VO: We called in the breakdown, and within minutes A1 Assist were on the scene. Tow truck driver, Derrick concluded a tow would be necessary. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: DERRICK: When you hit the pothole, the suspension is gone… VO: He was playing by the rules. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: DERRICK: Can’t just tow without an authorisation, we can’t just tow it to a yard, those scruffy companies aren’t here anymore. VO: He even called in his manager Marius to assist, he was also not interested in bending the rules. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER: OPERATIVE: I think it’s Execuline… MARIUS: We don’t tow Execuline – they only work with the AA VO: But without an authorisation, they were not taking the bait - it was time to tell them they had passed the test. BONGANI: we wanted to see if you guys would follow the rules, you guys did well, you passed the test… that’s a good thing. MARIUS: Yes, it is. Becaue of a handful drivers that make mistakes and con people we all get given a bad name. VO: While these towtruckers passed the test this time, we still had enough complaints against A1 Assist to warrant a visit to the big boss. Company Director, Rudi Steynberg agreed to meet with us at their storage yard. The company tows over 300 cars a week with almost 200 drivers on the road – he says these complaints are the exception not the rule. RUDI: You’re not on the accident scene, and we don’t always know what happens on the accident scene, like I said, there are a lot of people that think they’ve got insurance or they think they’re covered in certain cases and they’re not. VO: But that wasn’t Antoinette’s scenario – she had comprehensive insurance, but A1 Assist was not an authorised company registered with her insurance. RUDI: There should have been a tow truck driver’s and the registration on that invoice…. BONGANI: nothing, no number, no driver’s registration…nada…. RUDI: this is a case that I will look into, it’s not supposed to happen like that…. VO: He promised the same with Rainer’s case. BONGANI: It’s one thing to say you are going to look at these cases, but what actions are you actually going to take? RUDI: Bongani, I am going to take action right now in these cases. I will investigate the drivers, and I will have a disciplinary with the drivers VO: Garth says tow truck drivers are often the biggest culprits. Accident victims don’t realise that they not only have responsiblities but they have rights too. GARTH: You have the right to phone your insurance company to get another operator to come on the scene and remove your vehicle at the insurance’s costs. VO: But for people like Thami Madlala who had no insurance, his options were limited. Thami says he was relieved when the tow truck driver came to his rescue in January this year. THAMI: They gave me authorisation to tow your car.They would pay for everything as a third party claim… VO: Thami was told he would only be responsible one day’s storage at a cost of R350. THAMI: I got here with the R350 to take my car my back and then she told me I need to pay for the towing fee, administration fee… The lady then told me now, me I need to pay 8.7, 9000. She was like it’s either you pay the 9000 or you give us your car papers and we buy the car from you. VO: Unable to come up with the cash, two months later his car was still at yard, with his bill sitting at a whopping R30 000! We introduced Thami to Rudi. BONGANI: He came here the next day wanting his car, he still wants his car… RUDI: We still deliver a service, but R8000 is too much, we don’t charge that kind of money. I will have to look into myself BONGANI: This isn’t just one or two people – your reputation is on the line. RUDI: It’s unacceptable for me as well, as a member of the public, we’re a company that operates mostly in Gauteng, we are here to assist clients and insurance companies to clients vehicles to the right destination – that is our core business. I don’t want to be labelled with complaints like this VO: Rudi dealt with Thami’s complaint while we were still there… RUDI: we’re going to deliver, give you car free of charge… BONGANI: when? Today RUDI: YAH. VO: While Thami got his wheels back, there is an important lesson for consumers to learn. GARTH: so, it’s very important that people the responsibility that what is verbally agreed to is written down. You are signing a legal document for a contract to remove your vehicle. If that is verbally agreed – you’ve got nothing to fall back on, you have no protection. VO: For Rainer, it’s a lessson that came at great cost. RAINER: // other road users // must know that they must be very, very careful when they select a tow truck operator.Don’t allow any rogue to come and take your car away, you may not see it again. PROMOS 10 second promo VO: The tow truck industy is a quantity business, the more cars you bring in the more you get paid - opening the door for dodgy drivers to con accident victims, holding their cars for ransom. 15 second promo 1 VO: Dodgy tow truckers bend the rules secure the tow - conning accident victims to sign on the dotted line at the scene - then knocking them with exorbitant bills the next day. RAINER: Don’t allow any rogue to come and take your car away, you may not see it again. 15 second promo 2 VO: Some Tow truckers operate like vultures, targeting vulnerable accident victims. GARTH: They are very smooth, // and they can really lure you into a false sense of security. VO: We investigates a company alleged to fraudulently tow people’s cars and holding them to ransom.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We expose a tow truck company conning clients by towing their wheels fraudulently and holding them to ransom.
metadata.Summary: A1 Assist cons clients into believing they are authorised by the client’s insurance company to tow the smashed car. But when it comes to collecting your car for repairs, the truth is revealed… Your insurance has no record of the claim, and you’re being held to by A1 Assist – if you want your wheels – pay up!
metadata.Further information: BACKGROUND This seems to be A1 Assist standard operating procedure. We have at least 5 case studies of our own and an additional 21 cases on HelloPeter for the last year (some as recent as February). There is a clear thread – we’ve got your car, if you want it, pay up! INSIDER INTERVIEW I have an insider that will spill the beans on the MO, confirming this is a tactic used by tow truck drivers to secure business. CASE STUDIES Below are three recent and most relevant case studies that are willing to go on camera – they have all the documentation and pics from the accident scenes. Some even tried to take legal action against A1 Assist. CASE STUDY ONE RAINER WODRICH’s 19 year old daughter was in a car accident on the 10th of October 2015. First to the scene was A1 assist, Rainer’s daughter was being attended to by paramedics having hurt her back and was about to taken to the emergency room. “A-1 Assist Tow-Truck (but with Help-U 24 Signage) arrived on the scene within minutes, and offered to tow the vehicle. I initially refused, telling them I would need to get authorization from my insurance. However, I told the Tow-Truck operator who I was insured with. A few minutes later, the operator handed me his phone, and the voice on the other end told me that he had contacted the insurance company, and he had authorization to tow the vehicle. I did not take the details of the other person on the phone, but he repeatedly assured me that he had obtained authorization. I again asked the tow-truck operator about the costs, and he assured me that because they had authorization, the insurance would cover the costs. For this reason there was nothing filled in regarding costs on the Tow Authorization and Invoice document. I then asked the Tow-Truck operator where they were towing the vehicle to, and his response was the Roodepoort Assessment Centre, where the insurance assessor wouldcome to have a look. I asked him why, because I only have fire, theft and 3rd part insurance on the vehicle, and why could they not take it to my home, about 2 Km away, also in Randpark Ridge. His response was that he had to take it to the Assessment Centre in Roodepoort because the assessor will need to see the vehicle, no matter what! He absolutely refused to take it to my home.” When he contacted A1 Assist to enquire about whether the assessor had been to see the car and what the way forward was, a lady informed Rainer that there had never been any insurance authorization, and he would have to pay a release fee of R8,300-00 to get the vehicle back! He checked with his insurance company aand they insurance subsequently confirmed that they had never been contacted and there had never been any authorization given at all, and this was all my responsibility because towing is not part of the third party, fire and theft cover on the car. He eventually got hold of a manager named Hennie, and after much begging, got him to reduce the cost from the original R8300-00 to R5200-00, still an exorbitant amount. After the money was paid to him, they delivered the car at his home almost two weeks after the accient, but the battery was missing, the fuel tank was empty and the additional spotlights I had installed on the car, and which were not damaged, were gone! This is an unscrupulous bunch of people taking advantage of innocent people at their time of distress, and extorting money from them because they are unaware of the trap they are walking into. CASE STUDY TWO THAMI MADLALA… “I was involved in accident on the 11th of January and in less than no time, there were tow trucks around my car. I then told the driver of the tow truck that I don't have insurance and how much would it be if he had to tow my car. He then informed me that the yard charges R350 per day and that I can fetch the car the following day. when I arrived at the storage to inquire about the amount I need to pay, they told me it would be around R9000 because of a number of things like towing fees, storage, etc.” Thami’s car is still with A1 Assist and his bill is sitting in the region of R20 000.00 CASE STUDY THREE ANTOINETTE TILL Had an accident on Witkoppen Road on 29th October 2015. The A1 Assist tow truck driver pretended to call her insurance company to get an authorisation number. She was also handed the phone and spoke to some fictitious call centre person to confirm her details and get authorisation. The staff at their offices perpetuate the fraud by giving you a refence number for the tow, but it was later revealed that no authorisation was given. Her insurance would only pay R1500 and she was liable for the balance of R3500 of the A1 account. WHY ARE PEOPLE BEING CAUGHT? The tow truckers get a ficticious person to pretend that they are the client’s insurance company – often giving back details like the car make and registration number – these details would have been given to the so-called call centre agent by the tow truck driver. Believing it’s all legitimate, the client signs A1 Assist’s towing agreement, the car is handed over and towed away. Only when the client makes follow up enquiries with their insurance company it is revealed that they have been scammed and no claim or call to them insurance was logged. By then it’s too late and the client’s car is being held by A1 Assist and the only way to get your car back is to pay up! CAN THEY BE CAUGHT? I’d like to do a sting operation, faking a minor accident. I’ll claim that I drove through a pothole and it looks like the suspension is broken. We’ll call in A1 Assist to attend to the accident and let it unfold. We’ll go to collect the car the next day with presenter and cameras rolling. We’ll also take Thami Madlala with and try to retrieve his car. EXPERT INTERVIEW We’ll Interview the South African Insurance Crime Bureau about these kinds of cases to show how widespread the problem is and to get some advice for consumers.
